title: Borobudur is built in central Java
summary: Builders in central Java created Borobudur’s terraced Buddhist monument in the eighth and ninth centuries. Reliefs, stupas and the arrangement of its levels give architectural form to religious ideas.

citations.locator: Description and Outstanding Universal Value / Brief synthesis

claims.text: Builders in central Java created Borobudur’s terraced Buddhist monument in the eighth and ninth centuries. Reliefs, stupas and the arrangement of its levels give architectural form to religious ideas.
Eighth–ninth-century construction range from the institutional description.

The monument shows a distinctive regional expression of Buddhism. Comparison with other Buddhist sites should preserve differences in setting, patronage and form rather than assuming a single architectural tradition.
